display.title: Chai Elul: The Birthday of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe
display.summary_short: Why Chai Elul, the birthday of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe, is a day when the blessings of tzaddikim reach us in full measure.
display.summary_long: A four-minute talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, cut from episode 545 and broadcast on the eve of Chai Elul. Uncle Yossi explains that the 18th of Elul is the birthday of two great tzaddikim, Rabbi Yisrael Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe, Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi. Our Sages teach that on a person's birthday his mazal is especially strong, so he can accomplish more in Torah and mitzvos than on any other day. For tzaddikim, this means their blessings reach Klal Yisrael in full measure. Even after a tzaddik's life on earth ends, only the body is laid to rest; the neshamah lives on in Gan Eden and keeps helping Klal Yisrael, in body and soul, just as he did during his lifetime. Now, at the very end of the golus, we need the blessings of these tzaddikim more than ever, to pass the final tests and see Moshiach's coming with joy.
display.lesson: On a tzaddik's birthday his blessings are especially strong; connect to the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe on Chai Elul.
